newsitem.title: THAILAND: British woman to fly home to serve drug jail term.
newsitem.headline: British woman to fly home to serve drug jail term.

text.p: A British woman serving a 25-year jail term in Thailand for attempting to smuggle heroin will fly home next week to serve the remainder of her sentence, an interior ministry source said on Friday.
British police officials were due to arrive in Bangkok to escort Sandra Gregory, 31, from Halifax in northern England, back to Britain on Wednesday, he told Reuters.
"The Corrections Department will hand her over to their British counterparts on June 4th. She will fly home escorted by the British police," the source said.

Gregory was detained along with Robert Lock of Cambridge in February 1993, as they were about to board a flight to Japan. Anti-narcotics police found 102 grams (3.6 ounces) of heroin in her possession.
Gregory pleaded guilty but told the court that Lock had paid her to smuggle the heroin out of Thailand.
In February 1996, she was sentenced to 25 years in jail for heroin smuggling. A death sentence was commuted because she had confessed and Lock was found not guilty.
Her trial was given wide media coverage in Britain and in Thailand.

A special 10-member Thai panel agreed in April to a request by Gregory to return her to her home country to serve the rest of her term. But the actual extradition was delayed due to legal procedures, the ministry source said.

Gregory has already served four years and four months of her sentence. Under an agreement between the two countries, Britons who have served a certain amount of time in Thailand can apply to be sent home to serve out their sentences.
Six convicted Britons have returned home since the pact was signed in February 1991, the ministry source said.
Thirty-three British citizens, most convicted for drug offences are currently serving terms in Thailand, the source added.
